presidentialSuccession.name: Rodrigo Paz
presidentialSuccession.notes: Won Oct 2025 runoff; ended ~20 years of MAS rule.

supremeCourt.name: Tribunal Supremo de Justicia / Tribunal Constitucional Plurinacional
supremeCourt.appointmentMethod: Since the 2009 Constitution, high-court judges are chosen by popular election from candidates pre-selected by the (MAS-controlled) Legislative Assembly.
supremeCourt.fspEraChanges: The 2009 Constitution introduced popular election of top judges (held 2011, 2017). In Dec 2023 the Constitutional Tribunal extended ("self-prorogued") magistrates' mandates after elections were delayed — widely criticised. Partial judicial elections were held in late 2024.
supremeCourt.stillServing: Composition in flux through 2024–2025; the 2023 self-extended magistrates and the partial 2024-elected judges sit under the new (post-MAS) government — full roster to verify.

courtHistory.event: The historic Corte Suprema de Justicia sat in Sucre (the judicial capital); composition shifted across the many 20th-century governments and coups.
Appointed Corte Suprema under the neoliberal-era governments, with members chosen by Congress.

Morales's new Constitution replaced the appointed court with a Tribunal Supremo de Justicia and a Tribunal Constitucional Plurinacional whose top judges are chosen by popular election from candidates pre-selected by the (MAS-controlled) Assembly.
The first and second popular judicial elections seated the high courts; null/blank votes outnumbered valid ones, undercutting their legitimacy.
With elections delayed, the Constitutional Tribunal extended ('self-prorogued') the magistrates' mandates — widely criticised as an illegitimate power grab.
Partial judicial elections were held in Dec 2024; the resulting bench sits under the post-MAS government of Rodrigo Paz (from 2025).

supremeCourt.justicesNote: Bolivia's high judges are popularly elected; individual current members are in flux (2023 self-extension + 2024 partial election) and not itemized here pending verification under the new government.
